summary: Keys in minutes and OAuth install to other workspaces is self-serve; Slack Marketplace listing needs Slack review (timeline not published).

approval_wait.notes: Only the Marketplace listing is reviewed. Slack's docs publish no review timeline; 14 days is an unverified placeholder, not a documented figure.

prerequisites.item: Slack workspace where you can create apps
prerequisites.notes: Workspace admins may restrict app creation or installation.
Apps open to other workspaces must support SSL for OAuth redirect, interaction, options load and Events API URLs.

prerequisites.item: Public landing page with privacy policy link
prerequisites.notes: Required for Marketplace listing; must be public, not behind a login.

prerequisites.item: Public support page with contact method
prerequisites.notes: Required for Marketplace; responses expected within 2 business days.
Marketplace: data collected and use, retention, user access/deletion, and an email or webform contact.

prerequisites.item: 10 active workspaces or 10 weekly active users
prerequisites.notes: Marketplace apps below both thresholds are considered unsuitable.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: Create a new app from scratch or from a manifest and pick the development workspace.

steps.title: Configure scopes and redirect URL
steps.detail: Under OAuth & Permissions add an HTTPS redirect URL and the minimum bot and user scopes.

steps.title: Install to your workspace
steps.detail: Install the app to get a token for your own workspace. An undistributed app is limited to that workspace.

steps.title: Implement the OAuth 2.0 flow
steps.detail: Build the install flow, use the state parameter, store each workspace's token securely, and verify incoming requests with the signing secret.

steps.title: Activate public distribution
steps.detail: Complete the checklist in the app dashboard and click Activate Public Distribution to let other workspaces install via an Add to Slack button or URL.

steps.title: Submit to the Slack Marketplace (optional)
steps.detail: For broad or commercial distribution, prepare landing page, support page and privacy policy, then submit for review.

scopes.notes: Marketplace reviewers return submissions that request unnecessary scopes.

scopes.purpose: List public channels and basic info.
scopes.notes: Request only if the feature needs it.
Admins weigh requested permissions when approving installs.

blockers.issue: Workspace admin approval is required to install the app.
blockers.how_to_resolve: Request the minimum scopes and send the admin a clear explanation of why each is needed.

blockers.issue: Marketplace submission returned for unnecessary scopes.
blockers.how_to_resolve: Remove scopes without a clear, testable justification; move enhancements to optional scopes.

blockers.issue: Marketplace app considered unsuitable for low usage.
blockers.how_to_resolve: Reach at least 10 active workspaces or 10 weekly active users before submitting.

agent_can_do: Draft an app manifest with minimum scopes
Implement the OAuth install flow, state check and signature verification
Draft privacy policy, landing and support page content
Write justifications for each requested scope
developer_must_do: Create the app and install it in a workspace
Click Activate Public Distribution after completing the checklist
Host the public landing, support and privacy pages
Submit to and respond to the Marketplace review team

claims_evidence.claim: Undistributed apps work in one workspace only; unlisted distribution requires an OAuth 2.0 flow; Marketplace listing is the path for broad or commercial distribution.
Activating public distribution is self-service via the dashboard checklist; the docs mention review only for Marketplace listing.
Marketplace requires public landing and support pages and a privacy policy covering collection, retention, access/deletion and a contact method.
Apps with fewer than 10 active workspaces and fewer than 10 weekly active users are considered unsuitable for the Marketplace.
Marketplace apps must use the OAuth state parameter, TLS 1.2+ and verify requests with a signing secret.
Reviewers return submissions that request unnecessary user token scopes.
Non-Marketplace apps face stricter API rate limits on some methods than Marketplace apps.
The specific scopes listed (chat:write, channels:read, users:read) are accurate and none trigger scope-specific review.
